site_name: xAI Colossus 1 (Paul Lowry Rd, former Electrolux plant)
serving_utility: Memphis Light, Gas and Water (MLGW); TVA is the wholesale supplier
load_basis: Estimated total site consumption of about 300 MW in fall 2025, of which about 150 MW was bought from the TVA/MLGW grid as of October 2025 and the rest came from on-site gas turbines (WPLN, 2025-11-20). MLGW's 2025-05-05 update confirms 150 MW of grid service energized (8 MW from an existing substation plus 142 MW from a new one). Epoch AI separately estimates 340 MW of IT power from July 2025 on.
notes: Same campus as osm:way/1381264361. MLGW says xAI takes standard industrial service and has a signed agreement with TVA and MLGW to curtail grid use when demand is high. Grid portion is what matters for utility accounting: 150 MW confirmed. A second 150 MW increment (second substation, at xAI expense) was projected by MLGW for no later than December 2025 pending TVA board approval; I found no source confirming it was energized in 2025. TVA board approved the first 150 MW on 2024-11-07; site ran on temporary turbines before that. On-site turbines and Megapack batteries are behind the meter. Coordinates are Wikipedia's single point for the complex (35d03m36s N, 90d09m23s W) and agree with the inventory point. planned_full_buildout_mw is the total grid request, not IT capacity.

serving_utility: Memphis Light, Gas and Water (minor service only in 2025); bulk load self-supplied from xAI-owned gas turbines in Southaven, Mississippi
load_basis: Epoch AI estimate of IT power at its 2025-10-19 and 2026-01-13 observation dates (first compute cluster; Epoch cites the company's S-1 figure of approximately 210 MW of compute power). Satellite-based estimate, not metered load.
notes: Same campus as osm:way/1386926534. CAUTION on the inventory value: the 946 MW we carry is Epoch's June 2026 estimate, not a 2025 figure; Epoch shows 239 MW through January 2026. Start date conflicts: Epoch infers the first cluster online about October 2025, while Wikipedia says the first major cluster (about 210 MW) came online around January 2026, so 2025 operation is uncertain. Not on the Tennessee grid in 2025: MLGW's 2025-05-05 update says xAI had not submitted a final power request for Tulane Rd and was not using significant electricity there (options of 260 MW to 1.1 GW had been discussed); Epoch and Wikipedia say power came from gas turbines across the state line in Southaven, MS. Canary Media (2026-09-11) reports the TVA board approved a direct TVA grid hookup on 2026-08-20. No published street address or coordinates found in an allowed source; MLGW describes the site only as on Tulane Rd near the state line. planned_full_buildout_mw is Epoch's projected IT power for February 2027.

Same campus as osm:way/1213758201, osm:way/1294595615, osm:way/1312795639 and osm:way/1312795640. Utility: WPLN (2026-09-08) reports that Meta Gallatin buys electricity directly from TVA and that its load is confidential by contract; Meta's own info sheet says it worked with TVA to plan its energy needs. A 2020 Data Center Knowledge article says TVA built a 50 MW substation next to the site. I found nothing confirming a role for the Gallatin Department of Electricity. Load: no sourced 2025 figure. WPLN (2025-11-20) wrote that the campus was using up to 300 MW, but its 2026 follow-up describes about 300 MW as the expected full build-out, so 300 is recorded only as the planned figure. CAUTION on the inventory value: the Epoch AI entry behind epoch:Meta Gallatin (87 MW) tracks a newer building whose land clearing began September 2023 and which Epoch judges operational only in August 2026; it does not describe the original campus and should not be dated 2024. Start year: WPLN (2025-11-20) says the data center came online late in 2024; Meta's sheet gives only the 2020 groundbreaking. No street address found in an allowed source, so coordinates are left null (the matched records carry them).

Same campus as osm:way/708931343, osm:way/844389014, osm:way/1103333136, osm:way/1103333137 and osm:way/1470261550 (former Hemlock Semiconductor site). Start year: Google's site page says the data center officially opened in 2019 (the same page also says it was built in 2018); the inventory's 2017 for bi:869-0 looks like a generator-permit date and should be 2019. Utility: Google's 2015 announcement says TVA will be its electricity provider at this site. That supports direct TVA service, but no source I found states outright that there is no local power company (CDE Lightband or Cumberland Electric Membership Corporation) in between, so confidence is medium. Load: no sourced figure for operating load or IT capacity; directory sites list numbers that I did not use. Coordinates are from Wikipedia's Google data centers list (36d37m16s N, 87d15m47s W).

load_basis: Electrical capacity reported online in Bitdeer's December 2025 production and operations update: phase 1 at 37 MW (online, being converted to AI use with completion targeted Q4 2026) plus phase 2 at 49 MW (online, completed). Capacity, not metered average load.
notes: Crypto mine in East Knoxville; not in our inventory. WUOT (2024-02-02) reports KUB said Bitdeer accounted for 9.4% of KUB's total electric sales in 2023 and is its largest industrial customer after the University of Tennessee, and that TVA has an interruptible power contract with Bitdeer whose terms were redacted. Classed as special_contract on that basis. Wikipedia, citing Knox News (2022), gives 63 MW drawn as of 2022. No street address found in an allowed source, so coordinates are null.

load_basis: 12 MW immersion phase reported complete in CleanSpark's December 2024 update; the remaining 48 MW of air-cooled capacity was under construction in the February 2025 update with hashrate expected online early in the following quarter. Completion of the 48 MW is not separately confirmed, so 60 MW is the expected 2025 figure and 12 MW is the confirmed floor.
notes: CleanSpark's FY2025 10-K reports 234 MW operational across 11 Tennessee mining locations as of 2025-09-30 (three from the October 2024 GRIID acquisition, seven bought from Exponential Digital in September 2024, plus Jackson). The site-level figures in this file sum to 200 MW, so about 34 MW of the fleet is not allocated to a site here. GRIID's February 2024 release says the 60 MW site sits on a 15-acre plot it owns and that Jackson Energy Authority built a substation on the property. CleanSpark says the site takes part in TVA's demand response program. No street address found, so coordinates are null.

Group record covering more than one physical site because the purchase agreement gives only an aggregate; CleanSpark's release says each of the seven acquired sites is 10 to 20 MW. Serving utilities are not named in any source I could read (the power agreements are in undisclosed schedules), so they are left null rather than inferred from territory maps. Year first energized not found. A search result attributes a statement that the Tazewell mine can use up to 20 MW to an Exponential Digital manager, which would leave 10 MW each for Winfield and Oneida, but I could not open that source.

site_name: Merkle Standard Memphis (4545 S Mendenhall Rd)
notes: Lead only: operation in 2025 is not confirmed. WUOT (2024-09-17) reports a five-year MLGW agreement effective 2024-08-01 allowing up to 45 MW in low-demand periods and 5 MW at peak, and that the site was still under construction with no mining at the time of the reporter's visit. I found no later source on whether it was energized, so start year and 2025 load are null. Address is published (4545 South Mendenhall Road) but I did not geocode it, so coordinates are null.

site_name: Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility (Frontier), Oak Ridge National Laboratory
operator: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (UT-Battelle for U.S. DOE)
load_basis: Frontier's power draw as listed on the November 2024 TOP500 list (Wikipedia infobox; article body cites about 21 MW). Covers the Frontier system only, not cooling or other ORNL computing; Summit was decommissioned in November 2024.
notes: Government supercomputing center, not a commercial data center. Year is Frontier's start of early operations (delivered 2021, operating 2022); the computing facility itself is older. Serving utility left null: ORNL is widely understood to be a federal installation served directly by TVA, but I found no citable source in this pass. County is from general knowledge. Coordinates left null (the matched record carries them).
